draft.title: Groups facing difficulties
card: Some groups can face extra barriers in the criminal system. A barrier is something that makes it harder to understand the process, use rights or get a fair outcome.

may face barriers from past and present distrust of police and courts, and from a lack of culturally safe services. Courts can use Koori Court processes, where Elders and respected persons take part, for some offences.
may find it hard to understand questions, charges or court steps. In Victoria, the Children's Court hears most cases involving children, with processes made for their age.
People who speak little English may need an interpreter to follow the process. People with mental illness or disability may need support to understand and take part.
draft.remember: Some groups can face extra barriers, so the system may need changes such as interpreters, support and special courts.

a.q: Which situation best shows an extra barrier faced by a group in the criminal system?
opts: A newly arrived migrant cannot follow English questions
An adult is nervous because they have never been to court
A witness must wait in a corridor before giving evidence
A person charged with theft needs time to find a lawyer
a.why: The migrant faces a barrier linked to language and culture, and an interpreter may be needed. Nervousness or waiting can affect anyone, so they do not show a barrier faced by a particular group.
a.clue: Look for a difficulty tied to belonging to a particular group.

b.q: Sam, 15, is charged with an offence and does not understand the court steps. Which response best deals with the barrier he faces?
opts: Use the Children's Court, with processes made for his age
Let Sam work out the steps and skip any support
Move the case to a jury so that more people hear it
Treat his case exactly as an adult's case is treated
b.why: The Children's Court has processes made for young people, which helps with the barrier of not understanding the system. Treating Sam exactly as an adult would leave the barrier in place. A jury does not address his difficulty in following the steps.
b.clue: Which response changes the process to suit his age?

a.best: A newly arrived migrant cannot follow English questions

b.best: Use the Children's Court, with processes made for his age
